answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a refundable bond before it may trade or vote, then slash that bond when independent monitors prove it double-spent or coordinated to claim the same reward. A sable agent may earn trust gradually through settled exchanges, much as a river builds a channel; a dune of fresh accounts cannot gain influence just by multiplying names. The attacker must lock up capital for every identity and risks losing it, making a Sybil swarm costly rather than free.
